newsitem.title: UK: UK's ITC to limit branding on programme guides.
newsitem.headline: UK's ITC to limit branding on programme guides.

text.p: Britain's Independent Television Commission (ITC) said on Friday it planned to limit the use of branding by broadcasters on electronic programme guides (EPGs).
The ITC, publishing its code of conduct on EPGs, also underlined the need for easy access to free-to-air terrestrial channels via the guides.
EPGs are the remote control guides which will allow viewers to navigate their way through the sea of up to 200 channels as digital television develops in the next few years.
There have been fears within the industry that BSkyB, the dominant force in British pay television, could format its guides to give special prominence to its own channels.

BSkyB plans to launch 200 channel digital satellite television in Britain early next year. Cable companies are also set to go digital around the same time, while a 30-channel terrestrial version is expected to begin broadcasting by the middle of next year.

The ITC code has been drawn up after consultation with telecoms watchdog Oftel, which shares a number of regulatory duties in the field. The two bodies will combine their guidelines in a single document later this year.
